opened.information:
Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts
Title: Electronic Arts
Chunks: 4,5,6,7,8
## History
### 1982–1991: Trip Hawkins era, founding, and early success
For more than seven months, Hawkins refined his Electronic Arts business plan. With aid from his first employee (with whom he worked in marketing at Apple), Rich Melmon, the original plan was written, mostly by Hawkins, on an Apple II in Sequoia Capital's office in August 1982. During that time, Hawkins also employed two of his former staff from Apple, Dave Evans and Pat Marriott, as producers, and a Stanford MBA classmate, Jeff Burton from Atari for international business development. The business plan was again refined in September and reissued on October 8, 1982. By November, the employee headcount rose to 11, including Tim Mott, Bing Gordon, David Maynard, and Steve Hayes.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-Gamespy-15)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-gamasutra_history-11) Having outgrown the office space provided by Sequoia Capital, the company relocated to a San Mateo office that overlooked the San Francisco Airport landing path.

## History
### 1982–1991: Trip Hawkins era, founding, and early success
When he incorporated the company, Hawkins originally chose Amazin' Software as their company name, but his other early employees of the company universally disliked the name; as a result, the company changed its name to Electronic Arts in November 1982.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-Gamespy-15) He scheduled an off-site meeting in the Pajaro Dunes, where the company once held such off-site meetings.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-16) Hawkins had developed the ideas of treating software as an art form and calling the developers "software artists". Hence, the latest version of the business plan suggested the name "SoftArt". Hawkins and Melmon knew the founders of Software Arts, the creators of VisiCalc, and thought their permission should be obtained. Dan Bricklin did not want the name used because it sounded too similar (perhaps "confusingly similar") to _Software Arts_; however, the name concept was liked by all the attendees. Hawkins had also recently read a bestselling book about the film studio United Artists and liked the reputation that the company had created. Hawkins said everyone had a vote, but they would lose it if they went to sleep.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-ea-early-history-17)
Electronic Arts' original corporate logo, designed by Barry Deutsch, 1982–1999[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-Gamespy-15)

## History
### 1982–1991: Trip Hawkins era, founding, and early success
Hawkins liked the word "electronic", and various employees had considered the phrases "Electronic Artists" and "Electronic Arts". When Gordon and others pushed for "Electronic Artists", in tribute to the film company United Artists, Steve Hayes opposed, saying, "We're not the artists, they [the developers] are..." This statement from Hayes immediately tilted sentiment towards Electronic Arts and the name was unanimously endorsed and adopted later in 1982.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-ea-early-history-17) He recruited his original employees from Apple, Atari, Xerox PARC, and VisiCorp, and got Steve Wozniak to agree to sit on the board of directors.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-18) Hawkins was determined to sell directly to buyers. Combined with the fact that Hawkins was pioneering new game brands, this made sales growth more challenging. Retailers wanted to buy known brands from existing distribution partners. Former CEO Larry Probst arrived as VP of Sales in late 1984 and helped expand the already successful company. This policy of dealing directly with retailers gave EA higher margins and better market awareness, key advantages the company leveraged to leapfrog its early competitors.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-gamasutra_history-11)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-NGen11-19)

## History
### 1982–1991: Trip Hawkins era, founding, and early success
Promoting its developers was a trademark of EA's early days. Games were sold in square packages modeled after album covers (such as those for 1983's _[M.U.L.E.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M.U.L.E. "M.U.L.E.")_ and _Pinball Construction Set_).[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-gamasutra_pinball-20) Hawkins thought the packaging would both save costs and convey an artistic feeling.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-gamasutra_pinball-20) EA routinely referred to their developers as "artists" and gave them photo credits in their games and full-page magazine ads. Their first such ad, accompanied by the slogan "We see farther," was the first video game advertisement to feature software designers.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-NGen11-19) EA shared lavish profits with its developers, which added to its industry appeal.
> The Amiga will revolutionize the home computer industry. It's the first home machine that has everything you want and need for all the major uses of a home computer, including entertainment, education and productivity. The software we're developing for the Amiga will blow your socks off. We think the Amiga, with its incomparable power, sound and graphics, will give Electronic Arts and the entire industry a very bright future.
—Trip Hawkins,1985 Amiga advertisement[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-amiga-world-21):6

## History
### 1982–1991: Trip Hawkins era, founding, and early success
In the mid-1980s, Electronic Arts aggressively marketed products for the Amiga, a home computer introduced in 1985. Commodore had given EA development tools and prototype machines before Amiga's actual launch.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-amiga-world-21):56 For Amiga EA published some notable non-game titles. A drawing program _Deluxe Paint_ (1985) and its subsequent versions became perhaps the most famous piece of software available for Amiga platform. In addition, EA's Jerry Morrison conceived the idea of a file format that could store images, animations, sounds, and documents simultaneously, and would be compatible with third-party software. He wrote and released to the public the Interchange File Format, which soon became an Amiga standard.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-22):45 Other Amiga programs released by EA included _Deluxe Music Construction Set_, _Instant Music_[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-23) and _Deluxe Paint Animation_.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-24) Some of them, most notably _Deluxe Paint_, were ported to other platforms. For Macintosh EA released a black & white animation tool called Studio/1,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-25) and a series of Paint titles called Studio/8 and Studio/32 (1990).[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-26)

Raven Software, a subsidiary of Activision, is a video game developer know for titles like _Heretic_, _Hexen_ and _Soldier of Fortune_. The company has been instrumental in the _Call of Duty_ franchise since 2011, collaborating with Treyarch and Infinity Ward on multiplayer design, campaign development and ongoing support across mainline entries and _Call of Duty: Warzone_.
**Founded:**1997
**Headquarters:** Westminster, Colorado
Deck Nine Gamesis an independent video game developer specializing in narrative-driven adventure games and known for its entries in the _Life is Strange_ franchise, including _Life is Strange: Before the Storm_, _Life is Strange: True Colors_, _Life is Strange: Double Exposure_ and _Life is Strange: Reunion_. The studio has also collaborated with Telltale Games on _The Expanse: A Telltale Series_.
**Founded:**2002
**Headquarters:** Los Angeles, California
Infinity Ward, a Microsoft subsidiary through Activision Blizzard, is best known for the _Call of Duty_ franchise. Founded by former team members of _Medal of Honor: Allied Assault_, Infinity Ward continues to lead the development of _Call of Duty_ titles and works to define the first-person shooter genre.
**Founded:**2003
**Headquarters:** Tokyo, Japan
Square Enixis a digital entertainment developer and publisher renowned for game franchises including _Final Fantasy_, _Kingdom Hearts_ and _Dragon Quest_. The company develops and publishes games across console, PC and mobile platforms, while also operating manga publishing and licensed merchandise divisions.
**Founded:**1994
**Headquarters:** Burbank, California
Insomniac Games, a subsidiary of Sony Interactive Entertainment, is a video game developer known for franchises such as _Marvel’s Spider-Man_, _Ratchet & Clank_ and _Spyro_. Following its acquisition by Sony Interactive Entertainment in 2019, Insomniac actively develops a number of PlayStation-exclusive game titles, including _Marvel’s Wolverine_.
**Founded:**1991
**Headquarters:** Bellevue, Washington

Bungieis a video game developer best known for creating the _Halo_, _Destiny_ and _Marathon_ franchises. Founded in 1991, the company was acquired by Microsoft in 2000, became independent in 2007 and then was acquired by Sony Interactive Entertainment in 2022.
**Founded:**2016
**Headquarters:** San Mateo, California
Sandbox VRis a location-based gaming and entertainment company specializing in full-body immersive virtual reality experiences. Operating across five continents, Sandbox VR combines motion capture technology with original and licensed content — including Netflix partnerships like _Stranger Things: Catalyst_ and _Squid Game Virtuals_ — to provide in-person, group-play VR experiences.
Related ReadingVirtual Reality Companies to Know
**Founded:**1986
**Headquarters:** Bellevue, Washington
Valveis a video game developer, publisher and digital distribution platform known for the _Half-Life_ franchise and Steam, one of the largest oline PC and Mac game stores. The company has also expanded into gaming hardware with the Valve Index VR platform, Steam Deck handheld console and Steam Machine console.
Related ReadingMobile Game Companies to Know
**Founded:** 2012
**Headquarters:**Boston, Massachusetts
DraftKings delivers a portfolio of online sports betting, iGaming and daily fantasy sports products. Originally launched as a daily fantasy sports provider, it has expanded into a vertically integrated gaming operator and employs talent with expertise across technology, data analytics and sports to enable optimized customer experiences.
**Founded:**2006
**Headquarters:** Los Angeles, California
Riot Games, a subsidiary of Tencent, is a video game developer and publisher best known for _League of Legends_, _VALORANT_, _Teamfight Tactics_ and _Wild Rift_. The company has also expanded into multimedia entertainment, with the animated series _Arcane_ and additional _League of Legends_ universe projects.
Related ReadingIndie Game Developers to Know
**Founded:**2000
**Headquarters:** Denver, Colorado
Bet365 is an online gambling brand that specializes in in-play sports betting. Founded in 2000, the company supplements its sports offerings with casino, live casino, bingo and poker options for its more than 100 million customers worldwide.
**Founded:**2001
**Headquarters:** Frederiksberg, Denmark

SteelSeries, a subsidiary of GN Store Nord A/S, is a hardware manufacturer that makes gaming peripherals and accessories such as headsets, keyboards, mice, controllers and mousepads. The company has made an impact in competitive gaming since its 2001 founding, sponsoring esports teams including FaZe Clan, Evil Geniuses and Vitality.
**Founded:**2008
**Headquarters:** Chicago, Illinois
Iron Galaxy Studios is an independent video game developer that has worked on over 80 titles across multiple platforms, including PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch and PC. It is known for both original titles like _Rumbleverse_, _Killer Instinct: Season 2_ and _Killer Instinct: Season 3_, as well as for porting major franchises such as _Skyrim_, _Diablo III_ and _The Last of Us_ series on PC.
Related ReadingGaming PC Companies to Know
**Founded:**1986
**Headquarters:** Paris, France
Ubisoftis a video game publisher known for the _Assassin's Creed_, _Far Cry_, _Tom Clancy’s_, _Just Dance_ and _Rabbids_ franchises. Publishing games across PlayStation, Xbox, PC and Nintendo Switch platforms, Ubisoft operates through a network of studios worldwide and is even organized into specialized creative houses focused on distinct game genres.
**Founded:**2003
**Headquarters:** Irvine, California
Obsidian Entertainment is an RPG-focused game developer and subsidiary of Microsoft known for creating story-driven experiences such as _Fallout: New Vegas_, _Pillars of Eternity_ and _The Outer Worlds_. Founded by ex-Black Isle employees, Obsidian Entertainment initially built its reputation on titles including _Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II_ and _Neverwinter Nights 2_.
**Founded:**2000
**Headquarters:** Seattle, Washington
PopCap Games, a subsidiary of Electronic Arts, is a casual games developer known for creating _Bejeweled_ and _Plants vs. Zombies_. Its grab-and-play titles remain central to the gaming industry’s casual segment as a whole, delivering accessible experiences across mobile, console and PC platforms.
**Founded:**1979
**Headquarters:** Osaka, Japan

Capcomis a global developer and publisher of video games across console, PC, mobile and arcade platforms. The company’s major presence in the gaming industry stems from its portfolio of multi-million-selling franchises, including _Resident Evil_, _Street Fighter_ and _Monster Hunter_.
**Founded:**2007
**Headquarters:**Denver, Colorado
IllFonicis an indie game developer specializes in asymmetrical multiplayer games based on popular film franchises. The studio is known for horror survival and action titles including _Friday the 13th: The Game_, _Predator: Hunting Grounds_, _Ghostbusters: Spirits Unleashed_, _Killer Klowns from Outer Space: The Game_ and _Halloween: The Game_.
**Founded:**1986
**Headquarters:** Rockville, Maryland
Bethesda Softworks, a subsidiary of Microsoft, is a video game publisher is known for the _The Elder Scrolls_ and _Fallout_ franchises — expansive and intricate worlds that helped define the RPG genre. The company publishes games across RPGs, action titles, shooters and strategy games, including newer releases like _Starfield_ and further installments in its flagship franchises.
**Founded:**2010
**Headquarters:** Seoul, South Korea
DoubleDown Interactiveis a leading developer and publisher of digital games on mobile and web-based platforms. It focuses on developing social casino games such as blackjack, slots, poker and roulette, with its flagship title _DoubleDown Casino_ being played by millions of users worldwide since launching on Facebook.
**Founded:**1991
**Headquarters:** Richardson, Texas
id Software, a subsidiary of Microsoft, is known for developing _Wolfenstein 3D_ and _Doom_ (1993). The company is considered a large influence in establishing the shareware distribution model and modern multiplayer gaming standards, and continues to expand the _DOOM_ franchise with titles such as _Doom_(2016), _DOOM Eternal_ and _Doom: The Dark Ages_.
**Founded:**1984
**Headquarters:** Santa Monica, California

Title: Playing to Win
Chunks: 6,7
“We have a lean model, which allows us to scale as the business of esports scales,” Mereu said. “We run M80 as a linear business, as opposed to spending ahead of ourselves, which has allowed us to be selective about deploying capital where and when it is needed most … competition is the cornerstone of our business, and we’re leaning on that fandom to scale our global fan base.”
This year, M80 debuted competitive teams in professional tournaments for “Valorant,” “Counter-Strike,” “Rainbow Six: Siege,” “Rocket League” and “Street Fighter.” Mereu said it’s utilizing community data as well as new developments in technology to take advantage of emerging markets around gaming-consumer behavior.
The company announced an “innovation arm” called M80 Labs in May, which will explore non-esports ventures such as merchandise and blockchain products. With its seed funding round, M80 is planning to increase its team rosters as well as expand beyond esports into web3 application initiatives to advance fan engagement, including digital collectable items. The company said that its new partnership with Portal will empower these ventures and exemplifies the steps M80 is taking to explore web3.
“We will continue to watch out for high-growth opportunities that allow us to make a competitive splash while also growing and monetizing our fandom across titles,” Mereu said. “While our esports teams are having success at a global level, we are also shaping emerging markets such as influencer publishing, web3 and the creator economy. We’ll have more to share about our plans in the coming months.”
**SURVIOS INC.**HEADQUARTERS: Marina del Rey
YEAR FOUNDED: 2013
BUSINESS: Virtual reality video game studio
CEO: Seth Gerson
EMPLOYEES: 75
FUNDING TO DATE: $105 million
NOTABLE: The company is partnering with the gaming division of 20th Century Studios to develop a new game based on the “Alien” action-horror franchise.

Since its founding in 2013, **Survios Inc.**has been devoted to developing and publishing virtual reality-based games. While the studio has released a few original titles, such as “Electronauts” and “Battlewake,” it has also created several award-winning games based on popular franchises. Within the field of game development, Survios chief executive **Seth Gerson**said that the company sets itself apart from other local studios with its adamant focus on VR and how long it has been working with VR and spatial computing technology.
“Survios stands out from the competition through a proven history in producing and delivering a multitude of premium gaming experiences that have consistently topped the charts on all major VR gaming devices,” Gerson said. “The studio has been at the forefront of the VR gaming industry since the market’s modern inception, and through that success, Survios is the premier hub for innovation in the future of gaming and expanding beloved intellectual property universes to new mediums.”
Among Survios’ releases are “Westworld Awakening,” “Creed: Rise to Glory” and “The Walking Dead: Onslaught,” all of which are based on popular television shows or movies. The studio is developing a single-player game based on the successful “Alien” action-horror franchise, which will be available for PC, console and VR. The title is being developed in partnership with the gaming division of Century City-based **20 th Century Studio**, which produced and distributed the “Alien” franchise.
“Much like how **Riot Games** pioneered successful free-to-play PC gaming and cultivated a massive gaming community, Survios has been at the forefront of VR gaming since its inception,” Gerson said. “In the current landscape, major technology giants are entering the VR space … which underscores Survios’ perspective that the realm of VR gaming is being increasingly validated and substantiated by established industry players.”
Survios is looking to expand its team, form new partnerships to access more IP for game development and grow its user base to increase revenue.
“What truly differentiates Survios from its industry peers is its unwavering dedication to virtual reality as a specialized sector of the gaming market, one that the company believes is poised for the largest growth in the gaming landscape,” Gerson said.

## **New York Excelsior (OWL);****New York Subliners (CDL)**

**Associated North American team:**New York Mets
**Investment by North American team:**Majority stake from owner

## History
### 1982–1991: Trip Hawkins era, founding, and early success
For more than seven months, Hawkins refined his Electronic Arts business plan. With aid from his first employee (with whom he worked in marketing at Apple), Rich Melmon, the original plan was written, mostly by Hawkins, on an Apple II in Sequoia Capital's office in August 1982. During that time, Hawkins also employed two of his former staff from Apple, Dave Evans and Pat Marriott, as producers, and a Stanford MBA classmate, Jeff Burton from Atari for international business development. The business plan was again refined in September and reissued on October 8, 1982. By November, the employee headcount rose to 11, including Tim Mott, Bing Gordon, David Maynard, and Steve Hayes.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-Gamespy-15)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-gamasutra_history-11) Having outgrown the office space provided by Sequoia Capital, the company relocated to a San Mateo office that overlooked the San Francisco Airport landing path.

## History
### 1982–1991: Trip Hawkins era, founding, and early success
When he incorporated the company, Hawkins originally chose Amazin' Software as their company name, but his other early employees of the company universally disliked the name; as a result, the company changed its name to Electronic Arts in November 1982.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-Gamespy-15) He scheduled an off-site meeting in the Pajaro Dunes, where the company once held such off-site meetings.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-16) Hawkins had developed the ideas of treating software as an art form and calling the developers "software artists". Hence, the latest version of the business plan suggested the name "SoftArt". Hawkins and Melmon knew the founders of Software Arts, the creators of VisiCalc, and thought their permission should be obtained. Dan Bricklin did not want the name used because it sounded too similar (perhaps "confusingly similar") to _Software Arts_; however, the name concept was liked by all the attendees. Hawkins had also recently read a bestselling book about the film studio United Artists and liked the reputation that the company had created. Hawkins said everyone had a vote, but they would lose it if they went to sleep.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-ea-early-history-17)
Electronic Arts' original corporate logo, designed by Barry Deutsch, 1982–1999[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-Gamespy-15)

## History
### 1982–1991: Trip Hawkins era, founding, and early success
Hawkins liked the word "electronic", and various employees had considered the phrases "Electronic Artists" and "Electronic Arts". When Gordon and others pushed for "Electronic Artists", in tribute to the film company United Artists, Steve Hayes opposed, saying, "We're not the artists, they [the developers] are..." This statement from Hayes immediately tilted sentiment towards Electronic Arts and the name was unanimously endorsed and adopted later in 1982.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-ea-early-history-17) He recruited his original employees from Apple, Atari, Xerox PARC, and VisiCorp, and got Steve Wozniak to agree to sit on the board of directors.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-18) Hawkins was determined to sell directly to buyers. Combined with the fact that Hawkins was pioneering new game brands, this made sales growth more challenging. Retailers wanted to buy known brands from existing distribution partners. Former CEO Larry Probst arrived as VP of Sales in late 1984 and helped expand the already successful company. This policy of dealing directly with retailers gave EA higher margins and better market awareness, key advantages the company leveraged to leapfrog its early competitors.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-gamasutra_history-11)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-NGen11-19)

## History
### 1982–1991: Trip Hawkins era, founding, and early success
Promoting its developers was a trademark of EA's early days. Games were sold in square packages modeled after album covers (such as those for 1983's _[M.U.L.E.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M.U.L.E. "M.U.L.E.")_ and _Pinball Construction Set_).[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-gamasutra_pinball-20) Hawkins thought the packaging would both save costs and convey an artistic feeling.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-gamasutra_pinball-20) EA routinely referred to their developers as "artists" and gave them photo credits in their games and full-page magazine ads. Their first such ad, accompanied by the slogan "We see farther," was the first video game advertisement to feature software designers.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-NGen11-19) EA shared lavish profits with its developers, which added to its industry appeal.
> The Amiga will revolutionize the home computer industry. It's the first home machine that has everything you want and need for all the major uses of a home computer, including entertainment, education and productivity. The software we're developing for the Amiga will blow your socks off. We think the Amiga, with its incomparable power, sound and graphics, will give Electronic Arts and the entire industry a very bright future.
—Trip Hawkins,1985 Amiga advertisement[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-amiga-world-21):6

## History
### 1982–1991: Trip Hawkins era, founding, and early success
In the mid-1980s, Electronic Arts aggressively marketed products for the Amiga, a home computer introduced in 1985. Commodore had given EA development tools and prototype machines before Amiga's actual launch.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-amiga-world-21):56 For Amiga EA published some notable non-game titles. A drawing program _Deluxe Paint_ (1985) and its subsequent versions became perhaps the most famous piece of software available for Amiga platform. In addition, EA's Jerry Morrison conceived the idea of a file format that could store images, animations, sounds, and documents simultaneously, and would be compatible with third-party software. He wrote and released to the public the Interchange File Format, which soon became an Amiga standard.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-22):45 Other Amiga programs released by EA included _Deluxe Music Construction Set_, _Instant Music_[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-23) and _Deluxe Paint Animation_.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-24) Some of them, most notably _Deluxe Paint_, were ported to other platforms. For Macintosh EA released a black & white animation tool called Studio/1,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-25) and a series of Paint titles called Studio/8 and Studio/32 (1990).[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-26)

Since its founding in 2013, **Survios Inc.**has been devoted to developing and publishing virtual reality-based games. While the studio has released a few original titles, such as “Electronauts” and “Battlewake,” it has also created several award-winning games based on popular franchises. Within the field of game development, Survios chief executive **Seth Gerson**said that the company sets itself apart from other local studios with its adamant focus on VR and how long it has been working with VR and spatial computing technology.
“Survios stands out from the competition through a proven history in producing and delivering a multitude of premium gaming experiences that have consistently topped the charts on all major VR gaming devices,” Gerson said. “The studio has been at the forefront of the VR gaming industry since the market’s modern inception, and through that success, Survios is the premier hub for innovation in the future of gaming and expanding beloved intellectual property universes to new mediums.”
Among Survios’ releases are “Westworld Awakening,” “Creed: Rise to Glory” and “The Walking Dead: Onslaught,” all of which are based on popular television shows or movies. The studio is developing a single-player game based on the successful “Alien” action-horror franchise, which will be available for PC, console and VR. The title is being developed in partnership with the gaming division of Century City-based **20 th Century Studio**, which produced and distributed the “Alien” franchise.
“Much like how **Riot Games** pioneered successful free-to-play PC gaming and cultivated a massive gaming community, Survios has been at the forefront of VR gaming since its inception,” Gerson said. “In the current landscape, major technology giants are entering the VR space … which underscores Survios’ perspective that the realm of VR gaming is being increasingly validated and substantiated by established industry players.”
Survios is looking to expand its team, form new partnerships to access more IP for game development and grow its user base to increase revenue.
“What truly differentiates Survios from its industry peers is its unwavering dedication to virtual reality as a specialized sector of the gaming market, one that the company believes is poised for the largest growth in the gaming landscape,” Gerson said.

## History
### 1982–1991: Trip Hawkins era, founding, and early success
For more than seven months, Hawkins refined his Electronic Arts business plan. With aid from his first employee (with whom he worked in marketing at Apple), Rich Melmon, the original plan was written, mostly by Hawkins, on an Apple II in Sequoia Capital's office in August 1982. During that time, Hawkins also employed two of his former staff from Apple, Dave Evans and Pat Marriott, as producers, and a Stanford MBA classmate, Jeff Burton from Atari for international business development. The business plan was again refined in September and reissued on October 8, 1982. By November, the employee headcount rose to 11, including Tim Mott, Bing Gordon, David Maynard, and Steve Hayes.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-Gamespy-15)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-gamasutra_history-11) Having outgrown the office space provided by Sequoia Capital, the company relocated to a San Mateo office that overlooked the San Francisco Airport landing path.

## History
### 1982–1991: Trip Hawkins era, founding, and early success
When he incorporated the company, Hawkins originally chose Amazin' Software as their company name, but his other early employees of the company universally disliked the name; as a result, the company changed its name to Electronic Arts in November 1982.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-Gamespy-15) He scheduled an off-site meeting in the Pajaro Dunes, where the company once held such off-site meetings.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-16) Hawkins had developed the ideas of treating software as an art form and calling the developers "software artists". Hence, the latest version of the business plan suggested the name "SoftArt". Hawkins and Melmon knew the founders of Software Arts, the creators of VisiCalc, and thought their permission should be obtained. Dan Bricklin did not want the name used because it sounded too similar (perhaps "confusingly similar") to _Software Arts_; however, the name concept was liked by all the attendees. Hawkins had also recently read a bestselling book about the film studio United Artists and liked the reputation that the company had created. Hawkins said everyone had a vote, but they would lose it if they went to sleep.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-ea-early-history-17)
Electronic Arts' original corporate logo, designed by Barry Deutsch, 1982–1999[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-Gamespy-15)

## History
### 1982–1991: Trip Hawkins era, founding, and early success
Hawkins liked the word "electronic", and various employees had considered the phrases "Electronic Artists" and "Electronic Arts". When Gordon and others pushed for "Electronic Artists", in tribute to the film company United Artists, Steve Hayes opposed, saying, "We're not the artists, they [the developers] are..." This statement from Hayes immediately tilted sentiment towards Electronic Arts and the name was unanimously endorsed and adopted later in 1982.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-ea-early-history-17) He recruited his original employees from Apple, Atari, Xerox PARC, and VisiCorp, and got Steve Wozniak to agree to sit on the board of directors.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-18) Hawkins was determined to sell directly to buyers. Combined with the fact that Hawkins was pioneering new game brands, this made sales growth more challenging. Retailers wanted to buy known brands from existing distribution partners. Former CEO Larry Probst arrived as VP of Sales in late 1984 and helped expand the already successful company. This policy of dealing directly with retailers gave EA higher margins and better market awareness, key advantages the company leveraged to leapfrog its early competitors.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-gamasutra_history-11)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-NGen11-19)

## History
### 1982–1991: Trip Hawkins era, founding, and early success
Promoting its developers was a trademark of EA's early days. Games were sold in square packages modeled after album covers (such as those for 1983's _[M.U.L.E.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M.U.L.E. "M.U.L.E.")_ and _Pinball Construction Set_).[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-gamasutra_pinball-20) Hawkins thought the packaging would both save costs and convey an artistic feeling.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-gamasutra_pinball-20) EA routinely referred to their developers as "artists" and gave them photo credits in their games and full-page magazine ads. Their first such ad, accompanied by the slogan "We see farther," was the first video game advertisement to feature software designers.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-NGen11-19) EA shared lavish profits with its developers, which added to its industry appeal.
> The Amiga will revolutionize the home computer industry. It's the first home machine that has everything you want and need for all the major uses of a home computer, including entertainment, education and productivity. The software we're developing for the Amiga will blow your socks off. We think the Amiga, with its incomparable power, sound and graphics, will give Electronic Arts and the entire industry a very bright future.
—Trip Hawkins,1985 Amiga advertisement[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-amiga-world-21):6

## History
### 1982–1991: Trip Hawkins era, founding, and early success
In the mid-1980s, Electronic Arts aggressively marketed products for the Amiga, a home computer introduced in 1985. Commodore had given EA development tools and prototype machines before Amiga's actual launch.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-amiga-world-21):56 For Amiga EA published some notable non-game titles. A drawing program _Deluxe Paint_ (1985) and its subsequent versions became perhaps the most famous piece of software available for Amiga platform. In addition, EA's Jerry Morrison conceived the idea of a file format that could store images, animations, sounds, and documents simultaneously, and would be compatible with third-party software. He wrote and released to the public the Interchange File Format, which soon became an Amiga standard.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-22):45 Other Amiga programs released by EA included _Deluxe Music Construction Set_, _Instant Music_[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-23) and _Deluxe Paint Animation_.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-24) Some of them, most notably _Deluxe Paint_, were ported to other platforms. For Macintosh EA released a black & white animation tool called Studio/1,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-25) and a series of Paint titles called Studio/8 and Studio/32 (1990).[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts#cite_note-26)

“We have a lean model, which allows us to scale as the business of esports scales,” Mereu said. “We run M80 as a linear business, as opposed to spending ahead of ourselves, which has allowed us to be selective about deploying capital where and when it is needed most … competition is the cornerstone of our business, and we’re leaning on that fandom to scale our global fan base.”
This year, M80 debuted competitive teams in professional tournaments for “Valorant,” “Counter-Strike,” “Rainbow Six: Siege,” “Rocket League” and “Street Fighter.” Mereu said it’s utilizing community data as well as new developments in technology to take advantage of emerging markets around gaming-consumer behavior.
The company announced an “innovation arm” called M80 Labs in May, which will explore non-esports ventures such as merchandise and blockchain products. With its seed funding round, M80 is planning to increase its team rosters as well as expand beyond esports into web3 application initiatives to advance fan engagement, including digital collectable items. The company said that its new partnership with Portal will empower these ventures and exemplifies the steps M80 is taking to explore web3.
“We will continue to watch out for high-growth opportunities that allow us to make a competitive splash while also growing and monetizing our fandom across titles,” Mereu said. “While our esports teams are having success at a global level, we are also shaping emerging markets such as influencer publishing, web3 and the creator economy. We’ll have more to share about our plans in the coming months.”

NOTABLE: The company is partnering with the gaming division of 20th Century Studios to develop a new game based on the “Alien” action-horror franchise.

Since its founding in 2013, **Survios Inc.**has been devoted to developing and publishing virtual reality-based games. While the studio has released a few original titles, such as “Electronauts” and “Battlewake,” it has also created several award-winning games based on popular franchises. Within the field of game development, Survios chief executive **Seth Gerson**said that the company sets itself apart from other local studios with its adamant focus on VR and how long it has been working with VR and spatial computing technology.
“Survios stands out from the competition through a proven history in producing and delivering a multitude of premium gaming experiences that have consistently topped the charts on all major VR gaming devices,” Gerson said. “The studio has been at the forefront of the VR gaming industry since the market’s modern inception, and through that success, Survios is the premier hub for innovation in the future of gaming and expanding beloved intellectual property universes to new mediums.”
Among Survios’ releases are “Westworld Awakening,” “Creed: Rise to Glory” and “The Walking Dead: Onslaught,” all of which are based on popular television shows or movies. The studio is developing a single-player game based on the successful “Alien” action-horror franchise, which will be available for PC, console and VR. The title is being developed in partnership with the gaming division of Century City-based **20 th Century Studio**, which produced and distributed the “Alien” franchise.
“Much like how **Riot Games** pioneered successful free-to-play PC gaming and cultivated a massive gaming community, Survios has been at the forefront of VR gaming since its inception,” Gerson said. “In the current landscape, major technology giants are entering the VR space … which underscores Survios’ perspective that the realm of VR gaming is being increasingly validated and substantiated by established industry players.”
Survios is looking to expand its team, form new partnerships to access more IP for game development and grow its user base to increase revenue.
“What truly differentiates Survios from its industry peers is its unwavering dedication to virtual reality as a specialized sector of the gaming market, one that the company believes is poised for the largest growth in the gaming landscape,” Gerson said.

Title: Microsoft Unveils Xbox Live Heralding the Next Frontier in Video Games
Chunks: 0,1,2,3
**LOS ANGELES, May 20, 2002 —** Today at the Electronic Entertainment Expo (E3), Microsoft Corp. became the first video game company ever to announce a comprehensive online game service fully dedicated to fast-action, always-connected broadband gaming experiences. The online console gaming service, named Xbox
™
Live, launches in North America, Japan and Europe this fall for the Xbox video game system and ramps up with consumer beta programs starting this summer.
Xbox Live will enable all gamers to find their friends easily; talk to other players during game play through the Xbox Communicator headset; download current statistics, new levels and characters to their Xbox hard drive; and play online.
“Online technology is the next revolution in video games, and it will fundamentally transform gaming into a new form of social entertainment,”
said J Allard, general manager of Xbox at Microsoft.
“Together with our partners we will combine exceptional gaming experiences, a world-class service and a viable business model so all parts of the online ecosystem thrive.”
Jump-starting the online title announcements, Allard said Xbox Live will support five Xbox Live-exclusive games this year:
“Unreal Championship”
(Infogrames); and
“MechAssault™ ,” “Whacked!™ ,” “NFL Fever 2003”
and
“Midtown Madness® 3”
(Microsoft Game Studios).
To date, 60 game companies have committed to create games for Xbox Live, and at least 50 Xbox Live-enabled games are planned to release by the end of next year. Some upcoming Xbox Live titles include
“Shaun Palmers Pro Snowboarder™ 2”
from Activision, Inc.;
“Tom Clancys Ghost Recon™ ,” “Tom Clancys Rainbow Six™ RavenShield™ “
and
“XIII”
from Ubi Soft; and
“SEGA Sports™ NFL 2K3,” “SEGA Sports™ NBA 2K3”
and
“Phantasy Star™ Online” from SEGA® of America, Inc.
As the grand finale to the Xbox Live unveiling, Allard announced a lineup of games in the works for the future of the service, including
“Star Wars® Galaxies™ “
(LucasArts Entertainment Company),
“Counterstrike”
(Valve Software for Microsoft Game Studios), and future versions of Xbox original blockbusters like

“Halo™ ,” “RalliSport Challenge,” “Amped™ “
and
“Project Gotham Racing™ .”
With the service approach, Xbox Live is poised to deliver the most seamless, easy-to-use and consistent online gaming environment for gamers, developers and publishers alike. It was designed by gamers for gamers and includes features such as delivery of real-time scores and statistics so gamers can compare themselves to the best players in the world; quick and easy game launches; fast downloads; the ability to find friends online across games with only one click; and the ability to maintain a single identity across all games with a single password.
Microsoft is building four datacenters in Seattle and Tukwila, Wash., Tokyo and London in order to run a scalable, secure and gamer-friendly service. Xbox will assist publishers by managing the hosting, networking, security and billing so that game creators can focus on creating awesome game content.
Key, consistent features of the Xbox Live service across games include the following:
*   **Gamertag.** Gamertag is a gamers unique online ID for all games across the global gaming service.

*   **Friends list.** This feature allows gamers to find friends online and invite them to a game no matter which Xbox Live game theyre playing.

*   **Xbox Communicator.**
Voice communication is integrated with all Xbox Live multiplayer games and enables voice interaction with teammates and opponents. Key elements of this feature exclusive to Xbox include voice masking, global muting and parental control.
*   **Matchmaking.** QuickMatch enables players to enter a multiplay experience with a single button-click, and OptiMatch, an Xbox Live exclusive, helps them select games and opponents based on similar skill levels.

*   **High-speed content downloads to the Xbox hard disk.** Only Xbox offers console gamers the ability to download and permanently store both free and for-a-fee content that can include new levels, characters, missions and statistics.
Allard painted a bullish picture for the future of online console gaming and the promise of Xbox to lead the category.
“Within five years every important game will be online,”
he said.
“There will be new categories of collaborative and competitive console games that are possible only online. The ability to download new worlds, levels, characters, weapons, vehicles, teams, statistics and missions will change the way developers think about creating games, and will change the way gamers play them.”

“ReVolt,” a fun online racing game from Acclaim Entertainment Inc. Pricing and specific offers in regions outside the United States will be announced locally at a later date.
With a hard drive, Ethernet port and slots for the Xbox Communicator built in to all controllers, Xbox was designed by Microsoft to facilitate online play right out of the box. Moreover, with more than 20 online service sites and 270 million unique monthly users worldwide on the MSN® network of Internet services, and the No. 1 online PC gaming site with Zone.com, Microsoft is uniquely qualified by its resources and experience to lead the way in online console gaming.

Title: Sony Computer Entertainment America and Sony Computer Entertainment Europe Announce Introduction of Dynamic in-game Advertising
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4
**FOSTER CITY, Calif. & LONDON, June 4, 2008**– Sony Computer Entertainment America (SCEA) and Sony Computer Entertainment Europe (SCEE) today announced the introduction of dynamic in-game advertising on PLAYSTATION®3 (PS3). Marketers interested in placing advertisements in games for PS3 or publishers with available in-game space for advertisements are able to engage through advertisement distribution partners, with IGA Worldwide selected as PS3’s first partner. This partnership will serve to bolster the already rapidly growing worldwide in-game advertising industry, which is expected to grow 1,150 percent to $971.3 million between 2006 and 2011 according to the Yankee Group.
“The PS3 platform is primed to leverage the high growth potential of the in-game advertising market,” said Phil Rosenberg, Senior Vice President, SCEA. “Ads that are organic to the environment not only benefit developers and advertisers, but also create a richer experience for gamers.”
“PLAYSTATION 3 is undoubtedly the prime opportunity for the in-game advertising industry,” said Justin Townsend, CEO, IGA Worldwide. “Through this partnership with Sony Computer Entertainment, IGA can provide advertisers with a large and valuable global user base of 16-35 year old consumers with disposable income. With our standardized awareness-building advertising formats being delivered directly into people’s living rooms while they play, there are great opportunities for advertisers looking to engage through an entertainment medium outside of the traditional TV spot.”
PS3 provides advertisers with a direct avenue to reach the highly targeted, sought after gaming demographic, and has sold more than 12.5M units worldwide. DFC Intelligence forecasts that sales for the current generation of game systems will pass the 180 million mark by 2011, therefore, reiterating the potential for the in-game advertising market.

#### About Sony Computer Entertainment America Inc.
Sony Computer Entertainment America Inc. continues to redefine the entertainment lifestyle with its PlayStation® and PS one® game console, the PlayStation®2 computer entertainment system, the PSP® (PlayStation®Portable) handheld entertainment system, the ground-breaking PLAYSTATION®3 (PS3™) computer entertainment system and its online and network services PLAYSTATION®Network and PLAYSTATION®Store.
Recognized as the undisputed industry leader, Sony Computer Entertainment America Inc. markets the PlayStation family of products and develops, publishes, markets and distributes software for the PS one game console, the PlayStation 2 computer entertainment system, PLAYSTATION 3 and the PSP system for the North American market. Based in Foster City, Calif., Sony Computer Entertainment America Inc. serves as headquarters for all North American operations and is a wholly owned subsidiary of Sony Computer Entertainment Inc.

#### About Sony Computer Entertainment Europe Ltd.
Sony Computer Entertainment Europe (SCEE), based in London, is responsible for the distribution, marketing and sales of PLAYSTATION®3, PlayStation®2, PSP™ (PlayStation®Portable) and PLAYSTATION®Network software and hardware in 99 territories across Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Oceania. SCEE also develops, publishes, markets and distributes entertainment software for these formats, and manages the third party licensing programs for the formats in these territories.

#### About IGA Worldwide
IGA Worldwide, Inc. (www.igaworldwide.com) is the leading in-game advertising company with a proprietary ad serving network. The IGA Worldwide Radial NetworkSM enables advertisers to target millions of engaged gamers across a wide range of platforms and genres. IGA Worldwide was selected by Sony Computer Entertainment America and Europe as the first partner for the PLAYSTATION®3’s in-game advertising platform. The company has delivered campaigns for diverse brands such as; 20th Century Fox, Ben Sherman, Discovery, FHM, Hawaiian Airlines, Intel, Jeep, MTV, and T-Mobile. IGA Worldwide also provides strategic consulting services including integrated product placement and promotion through its dedicated creative solutions department. Headquartered in New York with offices in London and Berlin, the group is backed by Peacock Equity (a joint venture between GE-Commercial Finance and NBC Universal), Easton Capital Group, Intel Capital, Morgenthaler Ventures, KTB Ventures, Translink Capital, Presidio STX, LLC. and ITOCHU Corporation.
More information about PlayStation products can be found at www.playstation.com or visit the Virtual Press Offices at: presscenter.playstation.com or www.scee.presscentre.com.

Title: European launch line-up 2nd half 2008
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6
**London, UK – Aug. 22, 2008** - Glu Mobile Inc. (Nasdaq: GLUU), a leading global publisher of mobile games, today announced its roadmap of titles launching in Europe in the second half of 2008. New titles include games based on global brands from DreamWorks, FOX, Granada, Hasbro, Konami, Playfirst, Sony, Sega, Warner Bros., ZeniMax Media/Vir2L Studios, and 2 Way TRAFFIC, as well as original titles from Glu including sequels to some of Glu’s favourite titles.
“Our European line-up for Q3 2008 is by far our most exciting yet and fully demonstrates the strength of our partnerships and the quality of our studios," said Frank Keeling, MD of Publishing, EMEA, Glu. “Our partnerships with the world’s best film studios, console publishers and world-class brand holders ensure our roster for the remainder of the year is hugely rich and varied, combining immensely popular game shows, arcade classics, cult favourites, outstanding film and sports licenses and brilliant original IPs."
The titles launching in Europe in the second half of 2008 include:
**Beijing Olympics 2008™**
Go for the Gold at the Beijing 2008 Olympic Games! Feel the excitement of the Olympic Games as you compete in four popular events – 100m, Hammer Throw, 200m Individual Medley and Table Tennis. Set records and earn your place on the awards podium. Rich graphics, easy controls and two game modes will get you in the action. 32 countries represented in the only official mobile game of the Beijing 2008 Olympic Games.
Launched July 2008
**The Dark Knight™**
Play as Batman in The Dark Knight, the thrilling action game based on Warner Bros. Pictures’ blockbuster film. Batman fights to eradicate street crime in Gotham City using his advanced combat skills and an array of unique gadgets. However, things take a darker turn when a new reign of chaos is unleashed on the terrified citizens of Gotham by a rising criminal mastermind known as The Joker.
Launched July 2008
**Dewy’s Adventure**

Based on Konami’s Nintendo Wii title, Dewy’s adventure is a unique and innovative isometric puzzle game with a simple to pick up one-button control system accessible to all. The evil Don Hedron has descended upon the peaceful forest with Black Water and it's up to Dewy, a small droplet of water, to eliminate the terrible scourge and save the Tree of Seven Colours. Take control of Dewy by rolling him around the environment and using special elemental powers to take on the dastardly forces of Don Hedron.
Launched July 2008
**Little Britain**
Join all your favourite Little Britain characters in a series of wacky puzzle challenges - in Little Britain: The Mobile Game you don't just watch the fun, you're part of it! This game is a must-own for all fans of the hit television series including cult favourite characters Lou & Andy, Emily, Daffyd and Vicky Pollard. Featuring the catchphrases so often repeated on school playgrounds all over the country, it’s highly likely that if you own the DVDs you’ll be saying ‘I want that one!’
Launched July 2008
**Ice Age™: Mammoth Mayhem**
Manny, Diego, Sid and Scrat are back in their newest mobile adventure, ICE AGE: MAMMOTH MAYHEM. Based on the award-winning Ice Age™ films, the sub-zero heroes must work together to overcome their prehistoric world’s natural obstacles. Travelling across frozen tundra, icebergs, volcanic caves and green valleys, the unlikely team must help their smaller friends survive the world’s first migration!
Launched July 2008
**TRANSFORMERS: G1 Awakening**
After 4 million years, a volcanic eruption awakens the TRANSFORMERS. Now fans can battle as the classic TRANSFORMERS robots in a conflict based on the original “G1” animated TV series. Players can use the strengths of each AUTOBOTS character to defeat the DECEPTICONS in turn-based battles. With up to 23 unique playable characters, this game is MORE THAN MEETS THE EYE.
Launches August 2008
**Sushi Shuffle™**

Kanpai! You’ve got a bar full of hungry customers and they are all depending on you to deliver their sushi fix. Move sushi around the board to make matches and earn money. Match colourful seafood treats from a menu of 8 tasty fresh sushi. Fill up plates using combos, chains, and side dishes and soon your customers will be dancing with sake satisfaction! Successful Sushi chefs are bestowed with rich awards, including ancient sushi etiquette, so you’ll know which sharkskin to use with Mr. Miyagi’s fine wasabi!
Launches August 2008
**Super Slam Ping Pong!™**
In the spirit of Glu’s runaway hit, Super K.O. Boxing, Super Slam Ping Pong is a hilarious, over-the-top game that features a cast of wacky opponents such as Master Wu-Pong and the Gnarly Gnome. Players must keep an eye out for each opponent’s tell and weakness as they fill their Super Slam meter to unleash powerful slams.
Launches August 2008
**Wheel Of Fortune**
The legendary TV gameshow makes its way to UK mobiles, featuring puzzles devised by the makers of the show itself, customisable avatars, downloadable puzzles of the day and dynamic graphics and animations that capture the essence of the Wheel. With the Bonus Round, Mystery Round and Jackpot Rounds to navigate in solo mode or vs the wily computer opponents, it’s time to spin the wheel, buy a vowel and solve the puzzle!
Launches August 2008
**Lemmings Tribes™**
The timeless playability of Lemmings Tribes marches towards its mobile release. This real time puzzle game challenges the player to save a set number of Lemmings within specified time limits on a number of levels filled with devious traps using only the skills provided. This requires a combination of problem solving, logic and experimentation from the player. The Lemmings come from three different tribes. Classic Lemmings only have access to their original skills whereas the others two tribes, Space Lemmings and Medieval Lemmings have access to new skills for extra challenge.
Launches September 2008
**AMF Bowling**

Play as any member of an elite international group of professional bowling celebrities on their journey around the world in the AMF World Cup for the coveted Golden Ball! The game blends new styling and atmosphere with dramatic and rewarding, skill-based & online accessible gameplay, offering a competitive and fun mobile bowling game with rich 3D graphics for mobile players anywhere! With the new and revised one-finger play, a variety of locations and player selections, un-lockable features, live multiplayer or tournament options, AMF Bowling is better than ever! Bowl "On-The-Go" and take your bowling anywhere with AMF Bowling Deluxe for mobile phones!
Launches September 2008
**Afterworld: GLOBAL CONTACT**
A catastrophic planetary event known as “The Fall” has caused 99% of the world’s population to disappear, along with almost all technology. Welcome to Afterworld: GLOBAL CONTACT, the new mobile adventure game where survivors journey the world in search of their families, going from continent to continent, encountering daring adventures in cities such as Paris, Seoul, Sydney and Rio de Janeiro. Confront each challenge and battle your enemies as you struggle to create communication towers to allow the world to regain GLOBAL CONTACT.
Launches September 2008
**Silent Hill Mobile 2**
The smash hit Silent Hill series returns with the follow up to the critically acclaimed first mobile release. Building on last years hugely successful mobile game, Silent Hill 2 will be darker, scarier and more challenging and bring the dark and decaying environments of Silent Hill to life.
Launches September 2008
**Pro Evolution Soccer 2009**
The world’s greatest football game returns to mobile! Building on last years hugely successful and critically acclaimed mobile game, PES 2009 will be everything you’d expect from this blockbuster series- the most playable and best looking football game on mobile!
Launches October 2008
**Madagascar: Escape 2 Africa**
RUN FOR YOUR WILDLIFE! The official mobile game of DreamWorks Animation’s Madagascar: Escape 2 Africa! Roar into action as Alex the lion and earn your stripes as Marty the zebra, but when things get hairy, you may need to dance your way out of trouble! Chart a course for side-scrolling African adventure, fun mini-games and puzzles.
Launches October 2008
**QUANTUM OF SOLACE**

You’ve seen James Bond in action – but never like this. With cutting-edge technology, your enemies just got a lot more dangerous and they can not only destroy your cover, but also dodge bullets and stay in hot pursuit. Never one to be ruffled in the heat of battle, you’ll unleash a world of hurt thanks to a technologically advanced combat system that allows you to hurl bouncing grenades and fire projectiles from guns that actually damage the environment. Immerse yourself in the high-intensity danger of the world’s most famous spy with levels and settings taken straight from the new QUANTUM OF SOLACE movie.
Launches October 2008
**Call of Duty®: World at War**
Call of Duty: World at War thrusts players into the ruthless and gritty chaos of combat and challenges them to band together to survive the most harrowing and climactic battles of WWII that led to the demise of the Axis powers on the European and South Pacific fronts. The title re-defines WWII games by offering an uncensored experience with unique enemies and combat variety. Demolish enemy buildings, call in air strikes and utilize deadly new weapons like flamethrowers as you fight your way like never before.
Launches Fall 2008
**Bugs Bunny: Rabbit Rescue**
Help Bugs Bunny escape some hare-y situations in Bugs Bunny: Rabbit Rescue. Marvin the Martian, Yosemite Sam, Elmer Fudd and others have trapped Bugs in a series of devious puzzles. Players use logic and cartoon smarts to outwit Bugs’ legendary Looney Tunes foes and rescue the wascally wabbit.
Launches November 2008
**Who Wants To Be A Millionaire? 10th Anniversary Edition**
This 4th edition celebrates Millionaire's 10th Anniversary introducing innovative new features, new questions, and a chance to win real cash prizes.
Launches November 2008
**Space Monkey™**
Space has been consumed by Earth’s garbage and it’s up to one courageous monkey to clean up the entire cosmos. Gamers must help Space Monkey navigate the galaxy while avoiding hazards and taking down space enemies that get in his way.
Launches December 2008

**FOSTER CITY, Calif. & LONDON, June 4, 2008**– Sony Computer Entertainment America (SCEA) and Sony Computer Entertainment Europe (SCEE) today announced the introduction of dynamic in-game advertising on PLAYSTATION®3 (PS3). Marketers interested in placing advertisements in games for PS3 or publishers with available in-game space for advertisements are able to engage through advertisement distribution partners, with IGA Worldwide selected as PS3’s first partner. This partnership will serve to bolster the already rapidly growing worldwide in-game advertising industry, which is expected to grow 1,150 percent to $971.3 million between 2006 and 2011 according to the Yankee Group.
“The PS3 platform is primed to leverage the high growth potential of the in-game advertising market,” said Phil Rosenberg, Senior Vice President, SCEA. “Ads that are organic to the environment not only benefit developers and advertisers, but also create a richer experience for gamers.”
“PLAYSTATION 3 is undoubtedly the prime opportunity for the in-game advertising industry,” said Justin Townsend, CEO, IGA Worldwide. “Through this partnership with Sony Computer Entertainment, IGA can provide advertisers with a large and valuable global user base of 16-35 year old consumers with disposable income. With our standardized awareness-building advertising formats being delivered directly into people’s living rooms while they play, there are great opportunities for advertisers looking to engage through an entertainment medium outside of the traditional TV spot.”
PS3 provides advertisers with a direct avenue to reach the highly targeted, sought after gaming demographic, and has sold more than 12.5M units worldwide. DFC Intelligence forecasts that sales for the current generation of game systems will pass the 180 million mark by 2011, therefore, reiterating the potential for the in-game advertising market.

**LOS ANGELES, May 20, 2002 —** Today at the Electronic Entertainment Expo (E3), Microsoft Corp. became the first video game company ever to announce a comprehensive online game service fully dedicated to fast-action, always-connected broadband gaming experiences. The online console gaming service, named Xbox
™
Live, launches in North America, Japan and Europe this fall for the Xbox video game system and ramps up with consumer beta programs starting this summer.
Xbox Live will enable all gamers to find their friends easily; talk to other players during game play through the Xbox Communicator headset; download current statistics, new levels and characters to their Xbox hard drive; and play online.
“Online technology is the next revolution in video games, and it will fundamentally transform gaming into a new form of social entertainment,”
said J Allard, general manager of Xbox at Microsoft.
“Together with our partners we will combine exceptional gaming experiences, a world-class service and a viable business model so all parts of the online ecosystem thrive.”
Jump-starting the online title announcements, Allard said Xbox Live will support five Xbox Live-exclusive games this year:
“Unreal Championship”
(Infogrames); and
“MechAssault™ ,” “Whacked!™ ,” “NFL Fever 2003”
and
“Midtown Madness® 3”
(Microsoft Game Studios).
To date, 60 game companies have committed to create games for Xbox Live, and at least 50 Xbox Live-enabled games are planned to release by the end of next year. Some upcoming Xbox Live titles include
“Shaun Palmers Pro Snowboarder™ 2”
from Activision, Inc.;
“Tom Clancys Ghost Recon™ ,” “Tom Clancys Rainbow Six™ RavenShield™ “
and
“XIII”
from Ubi Soft; and
“SEGA Sports™ NFL 2K3,” “SEGA Sports™ NBA 2K3”
and
“Phantasy Star™ Online” from SEGA® of America, Inc.
As the grand finale to the Xbox Live unveiling, Allard announced a lineup of games in the works for the future of the service, including
“Star Wars® Galaxies™ “
(LucasArts Entertainment Company),
“Counterstrike”
(Valve Software for Microsoft Game Studios), and future versions of Xbox original blockbusters like

“Halo™ ,” “RalliSport Challenge,” “Amped™ “
and
“Project Gotham Racing™ .”
With the service approach, Xbox Live is poised to deliver the most seamless, easy-to-use and consistent online gaming environment for gamers, developers and publishers alike. It was designed by gamers for gamers and includes features such as delivery of real-time scores and statistics so gamers can compare themselves to the best players in the world; quick and easy game launches; fast downloads; the ability to find friends online across games with only one click; and the ability to maintain a single identity across all games with a single password.
Microsoft is building four datacenters in Seattle and Tukwila, Wash., Tokyo and London in order to run a scalable, secure and gamer-friendly service. Xbox will assist publishers by managing the hosting, networking, security and billing so that game creators can focus on creating awesome game content.
Key, consistent features of the Xbox Live service across games include the following:
*   **Gamertag.** Gamertag is a gamers unique online ID for all games across the global gaming service.

*   **Friends list.** This feature allows gamers to find friends online and invite them to a game no matter which Xbox Live game theyre playing.

*   **Xbox Communicator.**
Voice communication is integrated with all Xbox Live multiplayer games and enables voice interaction with teammates and opponents. Key elements of this feature exclusive to Xbox include voice masking, global muting and parental control.
*   **Matchmaking.** QuickMatch enables players to enter a multiplay experience with a single button-click, and OptiMatch, an Xbox Live exclusive, helps them select games and opponents based on similar skill levels.

*   **High-speed content downloads to the Xbox hard disk.** Only Xbox offers console gamers the ability to download and permanently store both free and for-a-fee content that can include new levels, characters, missions and statistics.
Allard painted a bullish picture for the future of online console gaming and the promise of Xbox to lead the category.
“Within five years every important game will be online,”
he said.
“There will be new categories of collaborative and competitive console games that are possible only online. The ability to download new worlds, levels, characters, weapons, vehicles, teams, statistics and missions will change the way developers think about creating games, and will change the way gamers play them.”

**FOSTER CITY, Calif. & LONDON, June 4, 2008**– Sony Computer Entertainment America (SCEA) and Sony Computer Entertainment Europe (SCEE) today announced the introduction of dynamic in-game advertising on PLAYSTATION®3 (PS3). Marketers interested in placing advertisements in games for PS3 or publishers with available in-game space for advertisements are able to engage through advertisement distribution partners, with IGA Worldwide selected as PS3’s first partner. This partnership will serve to bolster the already rapidly growing worldwide in-game advertising industry, which is expected to grow 1,150 percent to $971.3 million between 2006 and 2011 according to the Yankee Group.
“The PS3 platform is primed to leverage the high growth potential of the in-game advertising market,” said Phil Rosenberg, Senior Vice President, SCEA. “Ads that are organic to the environment not only benefit developers and advertisers, but also create a richer experience for gamers.”
“PLAYSTATION 3 is undoubtedly the prime opportunity for the in-game advertising industry,” said Justin Townsend, CEO, IGA Worldwide. “Through this partnership with Sony Computer Entertainment, IGA can provide advertisers with a large and valuable global user base of 16-35 year old consumers with disposable income. With our standardized awareness-building advertising formats being delivered directly into people’s living rooms while they play, there are great opportunities for advertisers looking to engage through an entertainment medium outside of the traditional TV spot.”
PS3 provides advertisers with a direct avenue to reach the highly targeted, sought after gaming demographic, and has sold more than 12.5M units worldwide. DFC Intelligence forecasts that sales for the current generation of game systems will pass the 180 million mark by 2011, therefore, reiterating the potential for the in-game advertising market.

#### About Sony Computer Entertainment America Inc.
Sony Computer Entertainment America Inc. continues to redefine the entertainment lifestyle with its PlayStation® and PS one® game console, the PlayStation®2 computer entertainment system, the PSP® (PlayStation®Portable) handheld entertainment system, the ground-breaking PLAYSTATION®3 (PS3™) computer entertainment system and its online and network services PLAYSTATION®Network and PLAYSTATION®Store.
Recognized as the undisputed industry leader, Sony Computer Entertainment America Inc. markets the PlayStation family of products and develops, publishes, markets and distributes software for the PS one game console, the PlayStation 2 computer entertainment system, PLAYSTATION 3 and the PSP system for the North American market. Based in Foster City, Calif., Sony Computer Entertainment America Inc. serves as headquarters for all North American operations and is a wholly owned subsidiary of Sony Computer Entertainment Inc.

#### About Sony Computer Entertainment Europe Ltd.
Sony Computer Entertainment Europe (SCEE), based in London, is responsible for the distribution, marketing and sales of PLAYSTATION®3, PlayStation®2, PSP™ (PlayStation®Portable) and PLAYSTATION®Network software and hardware in 99 territories across Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Oceania. SCEE also develops, publishes, markets and distributes entertainment software for these formats, and manages the third party licensing programs for the formats in these territories.

#### About IGA Worldwide
IGA Worldwide, Inc. (www.igaworldwide.com) is the leading in-game advertising company with a proprietary ad serving network. The IGA Worldwide Radial NetworkSM enables advertisers to target millions of engaged gamers across a wide range of platforms and genres. IGA Worldwide was selected by Sony Computer Entertainment America and Europe as the first partner for the PLAYSTATION®3’s in-game advertising platform. The company has delivered campaigns for diverse brands such as; 20th Century Fox, Ben Sherman, Discovery, FHM, Hawaiian Airlines, Intel, Jeep, MTV, and T-Mobile. IGA Worldwide also provides strategic consulting services including integrated product placement and promotion through its dedicated creative solutions department. Headquartered in New York with offices in London and Berlin, the group is backed by Peacock Equity (a joint venture between GE-Commercial Finance and NBC Universal), Easton Capital Group, Intel Capital, Morgenthaler Ventures, KTB Ventures, Translink Capital, Presidio STX, LLC. and ITOCHU Corporation.

**Paul Gardner Allen** (January 21, 1953 – October 15, 2018) was an American businessman, computer programmer, and investor. He co-founded Microsoft Corporation with his childhood friend Bill Gates in 1975, which was followed by the microcomputer revolution of the 1970s and 1980s. Allen was ranked as one of the richest people in American history by _Forbes_, with an estimated net worth of $20.3 billion at the time of his death in October 2018.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-Forbes400-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-3)

Allen quit day-to-day work at Microsoft in early 1983 after a Hodgkin lymphoma diagnosis, remaining on its board as vice-chairman. He and his sister, Jody Allen, founded [Vulcan Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulcan_Inc. "Vulcan Inc.") in 1986,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-4) a privately held company that managed his business and philanthropic efforts. At the time of his death, he had a multi-billion dollar investment portfolio, including technology and media companies, scientific research, real estate holdings, private space flight ventures and stakes in other sectors. He owned the Seattle Seahawks of the National Football League[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-seahawks-5) and the Portland Trail Blazers of the National Basketball Association,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-trailblazers-6) and was part-owner of the Seattle Sounders FC of Major League Soccer.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-soccer-7) Under the Allen Estate's helm, the Seahawks won Super Bowl XLVIII, LX, and made it to two other Super Bowls (XLIX, XL). In 2000 he resigned from his position on Microsoft's board and assumed the post of senior strategy advisor to the company's management team.

Allen founded the Allen Institutes for Brain Science,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-8)Artificial Intelligence,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-9) and Cell Science,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-10) as well as companies like Stratolaunch Systems[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-11) and Apex Learning.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-12) He gave more than $2 billion to causes such as education, wildlife and environmental conservation, the arts, healthcare and community services.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-Expanded_bio-13) In 2004, he funded the first crewed private spaceplane with SpaceShipOne.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-Collier-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-Airandspace.si.edu-15) He received numerous awards and honors and was listed among the _Time_ 100 Most Influential People in the World in 2007 and 2008.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-TIME-16) He also discovered the wrecks of various famous warships, like the Japanese battleship _Musashi_ and USS _Indianapolis_.
Allen was diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma in 2009. He died of septic shock related to cancer on October 15, 2018, at the age of 65.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-Inquisitr-17) Shortly after his death, in April 2019, the Allen-funded Stratolaunch first flew and became the largest aircraft in history by wingspan.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-ArsTechnica-18)
Allen (left) with Bill Gates at Lakeside School in 1970

Allen was born on January 21, 1953, in Seattle, Washington, to Kenneth Sam Allen (a librarian)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-19) and Edna Faye (née Gardner) Allen[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-more_than_money-20) (a fourth-grade teacher).[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-21) From 1965 to 1971 he attended Lakeside School,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-auto-22) a private school in Seattle where he befriended Bill Gates, with whom he shared an enthusiasm for computers.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-auto-22) They used Lakeside's Teletype terminals to develop their programming skills on several time-sharing computer systems.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-before_microsoft-23) They also used the laboratory of the Computer Science Department of the University of Washington for personal research and computer programming until they were banned in 1971 for abusing their privileges.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-24)
Gates and Allen joined with Ric Weiland and Gates' childhood best friend and first collaborator, Kent Evans, to form the Lakeside Programming Club and find bugs in Computer Center Corporation's software, in exchange for extra computer time.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-25) In 1972, after Evans' sudden death in a mountain climbing accident, Gates turned to Allen for help finishing an automated class scheduling system for Lakeside.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-leibovich20001231-26) They then formed Traf-O-Data to make traffic counters based on the Intel 8008 processor. According to Allen, he and Gates would go dumpster diving during their teenage years for computer program code.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-27)

## Businesses and investments

In 2013, Vulcan Productions co-produced the Richard E. Robbins-directed film _Girl Rising_[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-111) which tells the stories of girls from different parts of the world who seek an education. Globally, over 205 million households watched _Girl Rising_ during the CNN premier,[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-112) and over 4 million people have engaged with _Girl Rising_ through websites and social media. Through the associated 10×10 program, over $2.1 million has been donated to help girls receive an education worldwide.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-113)
Also in 2013, Vulcan Productions signed on as a producing partner of _[Pandora's Promise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandora's\_Promise "Pandora's Promise")_,[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-114) a documentary about nuclear power, directed by Oscar-nominated director Robert Stone. It was released on CNN in November 2013. A variety of college and private screenings as well as panel discussions have been hosted throughout the country.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen#cite_note-115)
